questions.q: Why can't WHERE filter directly on an aggregate function like AVG(ListPrice)?
options: WHERE is evaluated before GROUP BY runs, so groups and their aggregates don't exist yet at that point
WHERE can never contain any function calls
Aggregate functions are not valid in T-SQL
WHERE only works with text columns, not numeric aggregates
questions.explain: This follows directly from the logical processing order — WHERE filters individual rows before grouping happens.

options: Filters groups, evaluated after GROUP BY has formed groups and computed aggregates
Filters individual rows before grouping, exactly like WHERE
Sorts groups alphabetically
Replaces GROUP BY entirely
questions.explain: HAVING is WHERE's counterpart for groups — it can reference aggregate results because it runs after they're computed.

questions.q: What is the correct logical order of these clauses?
options: FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY
SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY
WHERE, FROM, HAVING, GROUP BY, SELECT, ORDER BY
FROM, GROUP BY, WHERE, HAVING, ORDER BY, SELECT
questions.explain: This is the actual evaluation order, distinct from the order clauses are typed in a query.

questions.q: Can WHERE and HAVING be used together in the same query?
options: Yes — WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters the resulting groups afterward
No, only one of them can appear in a single query
Only if GROUP BY is omitted
HAVING must always come before WHERE in the clause order
questions.explain: They serve different stages: WHERE narrows the raw rows first, HAVING narrows the groups computed from what's left.

questions.q: In 'WHERE Color IS NOT NULL GROUP BY Color HAVING AVG(ListPrice) > 500', what does the WHERE clause accomplish that HAVING couldn't do as efficiently?
options: It removes rows with no color BEFORE grouping even starts, rather than filtering after aggregation
It has no real effect and could be removed entirely
It filters groups by their average price
It sorts the results before HAVING runs
questions.explain: Filtering unwanted rows out early with WHERE means those rows never even factor into the grouping/aggregation step.
